description:
The Department of Middle East Studies (MES) at the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, is currently accepting applications to its M.A. program in Arabic Studies.

The M.A. in Arabic Studies at the University of Michigan is a two-year program that prepares students for entrance into a top-tier Ph.D. program in Arabic Studies or a related field; for a professional career in which expertise in the Arab world is a prerequisite; or to complement a professional degree (e.g., law, public policy, business, public health).

The program draws on the strengths of our distinguished faculty in Arabic language, linguistics, literature, and culture, and is enriched by the university’s renowned resources for the study of the Middle East, including the Islamic Studies Program, the Center for Middle Eastern and North African Studies (a Title VI National Resource Center), the an-Najah Arabic language program, and an extensive library collection.

The M.A. program has two tracks:

*   Track 1: Arabic Literature and Culture
*   Track 2: Arabic Language and Linguistics

Students on both tracks are required to complete a total of 30 credits (normally, 10 courses) and an M.A. thesis, an original research project of 30-40 pages written under the supervision of an MES faculty member. The degree requirements are flexible in order to meet the needs and interests of individual students. All students are required to take one MES course on literary and cultural theory and one on the structures of Arabic. Additional coursework is chosen from a list of MES graduate courses in consultation with the graduate advisor. Students who have not had the equivalent of five years of university-level training in Modern Standard Arabic must continue to take Arabic language courses. Students are also encouraged to study a second Middle Eastern language.
Program name: Master of Arts in Arabic Studies

description: The Master of Science in Community-Based Implementation Science is a 42-credit graduate program in the Department of Health Behavior and Health Education at the University of Michigan School of Public Health. This program addresses the significant gap between what we know from research can improve health and what is delivered in real-world community settings. Implementation science is the study of methods to promote the systematic uptake of research findings and other evidence-based practices into routine practice, and, hence, to improve the quality and effectiveness of health services. This degree trains students to lead implementation efforts for community-based health interventions and programs. Students will gain skills in community-based participatory research, implementation science, and program evaluation. Graduates of the MS program will be well-positioned to serve as research staff and program managers in community-based organizations, public health departments, health care systems, and other settings where health promotion interventions are delivered. The degree also provides excellent preparation for students interested in future doctoral study.
Program name: Master of Science in Community-Based Implementation Science

This unique combination of rigorous academics and real-world experience equips Ford School graduates to make a difference in the public, private, and non-profit sectors. description: The Master of Science in Quantitative Methodology: Social and Behavioral Sciences program is an innovative, flexible, 34-credit degree that provides students with strong quantitative research skills that are in high demand in the academic job market, private sector, and government. description: The Master of Science in Science, Technology, and Public Policy (STPP MS) is a 33-credit, 12-month program that prepares students to build careers at the interface of science, technology, and policy. STPP MS graduates will be prepared to take on analytical roles in government agencies, non-profits, and private sector organizations where they will analyze the impact of new technologies on society and of public policies on the development of new technologies. The MS is a STEM-designated degree program (CIP Code 44.0501). Unlike the Ford School’s MPP or MPA degrees, the MS degree provides students with a narrower, more specialized focus on technology policy. Admission to the MS will require a bachelor's degree in a STEM field, or extensive coursework and/or experience in science and technology. The program aims to recruit students from a range of STEM backgrounds, including students in the natural sciences, engineering, and computer/data science, who are interested in policy. Students will be required to develop a specialization in a policy area related to their science/technology background. The program’s curriculum will provide students with core skills in policy analysis and quantitative methods, as well as a deeper understanding of the institutional context in which technology policy is made. All students will take a common core of required courses, an integrative seminar that will bring in technology policy practitioners and researchers, a three-course specialization in a policy area of their choice, and a course in their area of science/technology. The 12-month program starts in August and is completed at the end of the following July.
Program name: Master of Science in Science, Technology, and Public Policy
